claims.text: The as-cast (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy has a coarse or uniform grain structure.
The unchanged alloy has poor crack resistance and load-bearing integrity.
The unchanged alloy exhibits a strong caloric phase-transformation response under applied-field and pressure-field operation.
Severe cold rolling of this alloy will introduce a high dislocation density.
Cold rolling followed by short annealing at approximately 0.9 times the caloric transition temperature will cause partial recrystallization and produce a hierarchical heterogeneous grain structure.
The resulting structure will contain nano-scale or ultrafine grains adjacent to coarser grains.
The ultrafine grains will be concentrated in high-strain or high-stress regions.
A heterogeneous grain structure produces nonhomogeneous deformation, strain gradients, stress partitioning, and internal back stresses.
Small grains constrain deformation in larger grains and promote dislocation pileups and strain-gradient hardening.
Back-stress and strain-gradient hardening will improve the alloy's tensile integrity and delay crack propagation.
The coarser grains will remain transformation-active and preserve the bulk caloric phase transformation.
The processed alloy will exhibit more than a 50% increase in uniform tensile strain relative to the unchanged alloy.
The processed alloy will have enhanced fracture toughness relative to the unchanged alloy.
The processed alloy's isothermal entropy change will remain essentially unchanged within experimental uncertainty.
The processed alloy's caloric transformation reversibility will remain essentially unchanged within experimental uncertainty.

The proposed integrity and caloric benefits will apply below the caloric transition temperature, near room temperature, under standard magnetic fields, moderate pressures, and conventional caloric-operation mechanical loads.
